findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/config.js::finding 2 can fire on a correctly configured repo whose committed run-state rule is not an enumerated spelling
findings.title: Finding 2 can fire on a correctly configured repo whose committed run-state rule is not an enumerated spelling
findings.action: Replace the enumerated text scan with a query of which ignore source actually covers the probe path and whether that source is tracked.
findings.disposition_rationale: CONFIRMED by repro. A repo with a committed root `.faff/runs/` line plus a present-but-untracked `.faff/.gitignore` is told `.faff/.gitignore` is the only thing ignoring run state and it is NOT committed, and a fresh clone gets no rule at all. Both claims are false: the committed narrow line covers the clone. Mechanism: step 3 passes because run state IS ignored, then `gitignoreMentionsFaffDir` only knows the 4 clean and 16 hazard spellings, so a narrower committed rule is invisible and the untracked-inner-file branch fires. It exits 1, which repos may gate on. NOT fixed here: `gitignoreMentionsFaffDir` is an explicit Chosen decision in the spec, and asking which source covers the path is a spec-level redesign rather than a correction of what was specified. Mitigating: the spurious warning's advice, commit `.faff/.gitignore`, is correct for any repo after FAFF-1299, so the cost is a redundant warning rather than wrong guidance. Recorded in <run-dir>/FAFF-1301/discovered-scope.json.

occurrences.title: Finding 2 can fire on a correctly configured repo whose committed run-state rule is not an enumerated spelling

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/config.js::selftest pins finding-1-only in a configuration that masks a double-fire
findings.title: Selftest pins finding-1-only in a configuration that masks a double-fire
findings.action: None required; the premise does not hold.
findings.refutation: config.js:2541 is `if (!faffDirGitignorePresent) return null;`, which returns before the tracked-ness branches the finding relies on. Verified empirically: a repo with a root `.faff/` hazard line and an untracked `.gitignore` emits finding 1 only, with finding 2 silent, matching the spec's table row.
findings.disposition_rationale: The finding reasons from steps 5 and 6 while omitting the `faffDirGitignorePresent` early return that precedes them, so the predicted double-fire is unreachable whenever no `.faff/.gitignore` exists. Confirmed by running the CLI in that exact configuration.

occurrences.title: Selftest pins finding-1-only in a configuration that masks a double-fire

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/config.js::the hazard remedy under-fixes the prefixed spellings
findings.title: The hazard remedy under-fixes the prefixed spellings
findings.action: Pick the replacement per spelling family, or note that the `.faff/*` substitution is root-scoped.
findings.disposition_rationale: Fair and accurate: for `**/.faff/` the scope-preserving fix is `**/.faff/*`, so the suggested line changes the rule's reach as well as repairing the hazard. The message is advisory and hand-applied, so nothing is automated on the wrong fix. Same family as the monorepo-intent observation already filed from the FAFF-1299 review. Recorded in <run-dir>/FAFF-1301/discovered-scope.json.

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/gitignore-ensure.js::widening the shared list also changes gitignore-ensure's shipped write-time warning surface
findings.title: Widening the shared list also changes gitignore-ensure's shipped write-time warning surface
findings.action: State the write-time surface change in the PR body so a later bisect lands here.
findings.disposition_rationale: CONFIRMED by repro: `faff gitignore-ensure` on a root file carrying `.faff/*/**` or `.faff/**/*` reports 0 warnings on main and 1 with this change. The direction is intended and the spec's superset-reconciliation rule is honoured, but the finding is right that the change was framed as a config-check addition only. Addressed by stating the write-time surface change explicitly in the PR body.

occurrences.title: Widening the shared list also changes gitignore-ensure's shipped write-time warning surface

findings.finding_id: test/config-two-file.test.mjs::the real-git oracle's committed parts are never actually committed
findings.title: The real-git oracle's committed parts are never actually committed
findings.action: Either git add the fixture files or rename the fixture to say on-disk rather than committed.
findings.disposition_rationale: Accurate and the finding concedes the verdicts are correct, because `git check-ignore` is index-independent, so every oracle row asserts what it claims. The residue is fixture naming plus latent brittleness if a future row came to depend on tracked-ness. Low value against the churn of touching 40 oracle rows.
